mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < previous and PAYEMS > previous in the same month
failure_condition: In a 60-day window with strong labor indicators, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% month-over-month indicates accelerating demand growth, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 10 such months, the SPX 20-day forward return is not significantly different from its mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 50 for two consecutive months suggests supply-side weakness, which can trigger a risk-off cycle and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: During such contractions, SPX 5-day forward returns show no significant negative relationship with INDPRO (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4%, it indicates a shift toward accommodative policy, which increases the expected discount rate discount and lowers S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns during this regime are not statistically lower than during tightening (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising payrolls (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE) creates a labor market imbalance that supports equity market optimism and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE <= previous month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: During such labor market imbalances, SPX 20-day returns show no significant positive effect (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in retail sales (assumed proxy via HOUST) exceeding 3% month-over-month, followed by a sustained decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL), suggests demand is growing faster than prices, which can support equity valuations and produce positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST month-over-month growth > 3% AND CPIAUCSL month-over-month decline > 0.2%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns during this pattern are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for the first time in 12 months, it signals a long-term labor market trend shift that historically precedes a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return in the subsequent quarter.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and UNRATE remained below for 12 consecutive months
failure_condition: In the quarter following the trigger, SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
